name: Version & Library Mismanagement
essence: The code you tested and the code that ships resolve to different library versions.

examples.summary: Payroll's February length stays 28 in a leap year; billing returns 29.
examples.mechanism: The two copies of the helper have drifted, so 2024 is not a leap year on one path (CWE-1104).

examples.summary: The resolver picks 1.4.0, which dropped the leap-year February.
examples.mechanism: Choosing the highest version changes behavior the tested 1.2.0 did not have (CWE-1395).

examples.summary: Payroll's February length stays 28 in a leap year; billing returns 29.
examples.mechanism: The copied helper no longer matches the one that was fixed (CWE-1104).

examples.summary: A caret range accepts 1.9.0, whose February is no longer a leap day.
examples.mechanism: `^1.2.0` allows any later 1.x, including a release that changed the calendar (CWE-1395).

examples.summary: Parsing 10 dollars yields 1000 because a scale flag is on.
examples.mechanism: Another crate's feature is unified on, so this binary scales amounts it did not ask to scale (CWE-937).

examples.summary: Payroll's February length stays 28 in a leap year; billing returns 29.
examples.mechanism: The copied helper no longer matches the one that was fixed (CWE-1104).

examples.summary: A caret range accepts 1.9.0, whose February is no longer a leap day.
Resolving to the newest published release selects 1.4.7 and a 28-day February.
examples.mechanism: An unpinned dependency installs a later build than the one that was tested (CWE-1395).

examples.summary: Two majors of the date helper disagree on February 2024.
examples.mechanism: Both copies are linked into one process and return different lengths (CWE-1104).

examples.summary: Billing February 2024 has 29 days and the copied payroll helper has 28.
examples.mechanism: The payroll helper is a second copy that dropped the leap-year rule.

examples.summary: Resolving the last published release picks 1.4.0, whose February is always 28.
examples.mechanism: The catalog is ordered by publication. The last entry is a later release, not the one that was tested.

examples.summary: Invoice code uses the v1 leap year and payroll code uses v2, which always returns 28.
examples.mechanism: Both majors are imported into one process and answer the same date differently.
